signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Safe-Haven Inflow
signals.text: CHF leads the G10 basket with a 1W average of +1.522% across 6 pairs, while AUD lags at -0.898% across 4 pairs, creating a 2.420% spread. AUD/CHF trades at 0.5507 against a 485bp policy carry advantage for AUD (RBA 4.85% vs SNB 0.00%, OIS basis +489bp). Elevated volatility with VIX at 28.3 and European equities retreating override the nominal yield support. In positioning, CHF leveraged funds hold net short -21,646 contracts (pctl 2, z -1.96), leaving substantial short-covering potential into safe-haven flows, while AUD/USD trades below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.6630 in a confirmed downtrend. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF; safe-haven flows override wide positive carry. Catalyst: Switzerland Employment Level at 07:30 UTC. Risk: VIX drops back below 20, halting safe-haven demand and reigniting high-beta carry.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Technical Level
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.18, holding directly above its SMA20 at 158.82 and SMA200 at 158.85. The 1M 25-delta risk reversal sits at -1.82, showing extreme put vol demand that explicitly hedges downside protection despite Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% offering a +269bp OIS carry spread (SOFR 3.92% vs TONA 1.23%). The 160.00 handle marks the key intervention watch level where Japanese authorities have previously escalated response warnings. JPY speculative positioning shows net short -29,545 contracts at the 85th percentile of its 52-week range, reflecting crowded short exposure vulnerable to any policy defense. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; options skew heavily favors downside protection near key resistance. Catalyst: Japan Tokyo CPI at 23:30 UTC. Risk: A clean daily close above 160.00 without official response drives short-covering toward 162.00.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Hawkish Repricing vs Technical Downtrend
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3117, contained below its descending SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3269, 1.3280, 1.3395) in an established counter-trend pullback inside a larger downtrend. Bank of England Governor Bailey noted the likelihood of additional rate increases if energy costs stay elevated, while Catherine Mann argued for hiking sooner. BoE at 4.00% matches the Fed at 4.00%, offering a neutral policy carry differential (+0bp nominal, -6bp OIS basis). Leveraged funds trimmed net longs by -11,856 contracts WoW to +23,730, highlighting institutional hesitation to chase the policy rhetoric ahead of US data strength. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD; overhead moving average resistance caps hawkish policy repricing. Catalyst: US Goods Trade Balance at 13:30 UTC. Risk: A sustained breakout and close above the SMA50 at 1.3280 shifts the technical structure to neutral.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short at Cycle Extremes
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.0978, holding below its SMA20 (1.1085) and SMA200 (1.1496) in a firm daily downtrend. CFTC data shows leveraged funds net short -105,891 contracts (2nd percentile, z -1.68) after adding -7,287 contracts WoW, signaling stretched institutional positioning. Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% maintains a +135bp carry premium supporting USD (SOFR 3.92% vs €STR 2.44% at +148bp). Meanwhile, 1M implied volatility trades at 6.5% against 30-day realized volatility of 5.4%, leaving a moderate 1.2-point volatility risk premium. Trade bias: Neutral/range EUR/USD; stretched short positioning limits fresh selling momentum into rate support. Catalyst: France and Spain CPI prints at 07:45–08:00 UTC. Risk: US data outperformance expands the 2Y yield gap beyond -160bp and forces EUR/USD through 1.0900.
